texts: bad: the parse links Sailsworn to the Council as a part-of-the-group fact but never records the clause's own claim that he is a member, so "is Sailsworn a member?" finds nothing. Turning the premodifier into an of-phrase makes the predicate unmissable while keeping the same meaning: "Sailsworn is a member of the Council."

mixed: the wardenship, the "for the current year" timing and the plain "is a warden" fact are all recorded, but "Salt-bloom Warden" is split so that the Salt-bloom link hangs off the reified state rather than off Sailsworn, and the very same title is treated as one single proper name in the next sentence - so the two sentences never join up. Lowercasing the job word settles the routing (a lowercase common noun next to a capitalised name is never absorbed into the name): "Sailsworn is the Salt-bloom warden for the current year.", and use that same casing wherever the title recurs. Note that the definite "the", marking a one-per-year office, has no carrier either way, so that shade of meaning is lost whatever you write.

mixed: the parse was judged acceptable and the leading, the warden and the tide-pools are all present, but the three-part modifier "new-moon harvest expeditions" collapses into one opaque compound whose only visible genus is "expedition" - nothing records that these are harvest trips or that they fall at the new moon - and the destination attaches to the expeditions rather than to the leading. Unstacking the modifier and giving the timing its own adjunct fixes the buried content: "At the new moon, the Salt-bloom warden leads the harvest expeditions to the tide-pools."

mixed: everything is right except that the fused compound "cliff-climber" is never linked to plain "climber", so "is Sailsworn a climber?" finds nothing; the wording itself is fine and the missing link is a translator slip rather than a phrasing problem. If you want the plain kind to bind without waiting on that fix, write "Sailsworn is reliable and climbs cliffs."
